column3: LightRAG is a RAG system combining graph-based text indexing with a dual-level retrieval framework, addressing three challenges: comprehensive retrieval, retrieval efficiency, and fast adaptation to new data; experiments show it outperforms NaiveRAG, HyDE, RQ-RAG, and GraphRAG across multiple datasets 2410.05779v3.pdf
column4: Page 2, Introduction section, the three bullet points starting with "In summary, the key contributions of this work are highlighted as follows"

column3: Both use graph-based retrieval, but LightRAG consistently outperforms GraphRAG on large datasets like Agriculture, CS, and Legal (win rates ~51-64%), with the biggest edge in Diversity; GraphRAG requires traversing communities causing many API calls and full community reconstruction on updates, while LightRAG needs only one API call per query and updates incrementally without rebuilding 2410.05779v3.pdf
column4: Page 7, Section 4.2 "LightRAG's Superiority over GraphRAG"; cost comparison on pages 9-10, Section 4.5 and Figure 2

column2: (Assignment Q3) Performance of ablated versions of LightRAG
column3: The -High (removes high-level retrieval) and -Low (removes low-level retrieval) variants both show performance drops; the -Origin variant (removes raw text, keeps only graph) shows no significant decline and even improves on Agriculture and Mix, showing the graph index already captures key info effectively; the full Hybrid mode (LightRAG) achieves the most balanced performance

column2: What three key challenges does LightRAG's architecture address?
column3: i) Comprehensive Information Retrieval ii) Enhanced Retrieval Efficiency iii) Rapid Adaptation to New Data

column2: What are the two levels in LightRAG's dual-level retrieval paradigm, and what does each handle?
column3: Low-Level Retrieval focuses on precise information about specific entities and their relationships; High-Level Retrieval addresses broader topics and themes, aggregating information across related entities

column2: Which LLM does LightRAG use by default in the experiments?

column2: Which four datasets were used for evaluation, and what domains do they cover?
column3: Agriculture, CS (computer science), Legal, and Mix (literary, biographical, philosophical texts)

column2: How does LightRAG handle incremental knowledge base updates compared to GraphRAG?
column3: LightRAG processes new documents with the same indexing steps and merges the new node/edge sets into the existing graph without rebuilding; GraphRAG must dismantle its community structure and fully regenerate it, costing about 1,399?2?5,000 tokens

column2: What three main functions are used in LightRAG's graph-based text indexing?
column3: R(·): extracts entities and relationships; P(·): LLM profiling to generate key-value pairs; D(·): deduplication to merge identical entities/relations
